title: How Venezuela Bondholders Finally Ran Out of Time - Bloomberg
主要内容: Venezuela's bondholders are facing a critical moment as the country approaches a potential default. President Nicolas Maduro announced on November 2 that Venezuela will seek to restructure its global debt following a final payment by state oil company PDVSA. The decision comes amid U.S. sanctions, which Maduro claims are the reason for the country's financial difficulties. These sanctions were imposed due to Venezuela's increasingly anti-democratic actions, including efforts to rewrite the constitution and reduce congressional power. Despite the challenges, Venezuela has historically managed to pay its debts, offering investors strong returns. However, the future remains uncertain. If Venezuela fails to meet its obligations, its international oil assets, including PDVSA's offshore refineries and oil receivables, could be at risk of seizure or legal entanglement. PDVSA's Houston-based refining arm, Citgo Holding Inc., has also been used as collateral for some bonds. If creditors pursue these assets, buyers of Venezuela's crude oil may shift to other sources, impacting both demand and prices.
